extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers and creative writers interested in character, metaphor, and dark/horror themes
extracted.subtask_description: Practical craft advice for creating active, memorable characters and strong, original metaphors, with guidance on using fear/darkness to drive narrative. Aimed at fiction writers working on novels or short stories, especially those exploring darker material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorable Characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters must be active and interesting; "they have to do stuff." Avoid the passive "everyman vibe" — it tends toward boredom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show characters through action rather than passive description. Use moments that reveal character via choices and behavior; avoid protagonists who merely react or blend into the background. (Example: Miriam Black — a character whose power to perceive how people will die shapes every decision, creating constant psychological tension.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a 'Save the Cat' moment to reveal character
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a 'Save the Cat' moment to show ethos, wants, and desires in action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a concrete, often small action early on that demonstrates who the character is and what they want; this moment communicates values and stakes efficiently. Treat this as a practical technique for making characters vivid and relatable rather than telling the reader about traits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crafting Effective Metaphors
rubrics_metrics.description: Metaphors are "like fingerprints" — they reveal how the author's mind works. Strong metaphors combine "two things that don't belong together." Metaphors must work both visually and emotionally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for surprising, original comparisons that convey both image and feeling. Draw on unusual observation (anecdote: mistaking a rock for a wounded bird) to see things differently and generate fresh metaphors. Practice the 'metaphor muscle' regularly to strengthen this aspect of your writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing Dark Content / Using Fear to Drive Narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Fear naturally drives compelling narratives. "Every novel is, in its core, a horror story" — writers help audiences confront universal anxieties through characters' struggles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame conflicts and character arcs around fears and anxieties to create emotional stakes; use horror elements not just for shock but to externalize and explore universal concerns. Treat darkness as a tool to deepen character choices and thematic resonance.
